title: Antilithiasic Potential of Herniaria hirsuta and Plantago albicans Extracts: Litholytic Effects and Their Use in Algerian Traditional Medicine
content: AbstractBackground: Urolithiasis, or kidney stone disease, is a prevalent and recurrent condition with significant healthcare implications. Conventional treatments, including pharmacological and surgical interventions, are often costly, have side effects, and face limitations. Traditional medicine offers a complementary approach, with plants like Herniaria hirsuta and Plantago albicans historically used for their diuretic and antilithiasic properties.Objective: This study evaluates the antilithiasic potential of aqueous extracts from Herniaria hirsuta and Plantago albicans, focusing on their ability to dissolve kidney stones in vitro.Methods: The plants were harvested from the Tessala region of Algeria and identified through botanical and microscopic analyses. Aqueous extracts were prepared by decoction, and their phytochemical profiles were assessed for bioactive compounds like flavonoids, tannins, coumarins, and saponins. Dissolution tests were conducted on kidney stones collected from patients, with their composition confirmed via FT-IR spectroscopy. Weight loss of the stones after exposure to the extracts was measured to calculate dissolution rates.Results: Phytochemical screening revealed the presence of flavonoids, tannins, and coumarins in both extracts, with saponins predominantly abundant in Herniaria hirsuta. FT-IR analysis identified various stone compositions, including uric acid, calcium oxalate, calcium phosphate, cystine, and struvite. The extracts exhibited significant litholytic activity, with Herniaria hirsuta showing a pronounced effect on cystine, uric acid, and calcium oxalate stones, while Plantago albicans was most effective on cystine and struvite stones.Conclusion: The findings support the traditional use of Herniaria hirsuta and Plantago albicans in managing urolithiasis. Their efficacy, particularly in dissolving cystine and uric acid stones, highlights their potential as cost-effective and natural therapeutic alternatives to conventional treatments. Further in vivo studies are warranted to validate these results and explore their clinical applications.
